queue.title: NEM Test report prompt: make the prompt safe to edit and lift the token limit
queue.description: In the live /verify workflow the Anthropic system prompt is a single-quoted JavaScript string literal inside the Generate Report node's jsonBody expression, so the first apostrophe or newline in Alex's real prompt breaks the node silently (the browser already got its 302). Move the prompt into a Report Prompt Set node as a plain fixed-value string so JSON.stringify handles all escaping. Also lift max_tokens from the live value of 1024 to the intended 8000, switch $json references to explicit $('Validate Token') references, and re-sync the repo workflow JSON to live. Prerequisite for any mechanism that lets the client edit the prompt himself.
queue.note: APPLIED TO LIVE 2026-08-13, CONFIRMED 2026-08-18. The 2026-08-11 note below was wrong by the time anyone read it: the fix was applied by hand in the n8n UI on 13 Aug (workflow updatedAt 15:03:50Z; execution 45 at 15:02 already shows Report Prompt in its path), so no commit in this repo recorded it and every doc still said PREPARED, NOT APPLIED. Found by taking the pre-apply snapshot: the live pull came back with a node the repo copy did not have. DO NOT re-send partial-update.operations.json - it would add a second Report Prompt node or fail. Verified live: Report Prompt is a Set node typeVersion 3.5 with no legacy parameters.fields, holding systemPrompt as a fixed value that does not start with '='; Valid? true branch fans out to Respond Confirmed, Mark Consumed and Report Prompt so the 302 does not wait on the report chain; Generate Report reads the Set node, uses $('Validate Token') references and max_tokens 8000. queue.title: Answer clicks during the question fade are swallowed and the quiz does not advance
queue.description: Found 2026-08-19 while fixing the acceptance suite. Clicking an answer while the fade between questions is still running does nothing - the question does not advance and the user has to press again. It reads as a dead click, on the primary interaction of a twenty-question quiz, so some drop-off may be attributable to it. It was invisible until now because the acceptance helpers slept a flat 600ms after every click instead of waiting for the question to change; the blind sleep absorbed the lost click silently. The fix belongs in nem-test-phase-b.tsx - either keep the answer buttons live through the transition, or queue a click that arrives mid-fade and apply it when the transition ends. tests/acceptance/nem-test-conclusion-logic-v2.spec.js currently retries the click once and says so in a comment; remove that retry once the component handles it.
queue.note: Fixed and merged 2026-08-20 (PR #11, d5edb65). Reading the component rather than the symptom turned up a SECOND defect the failures report had not separated out: selectAnswer was also re-entrant, so a second click inside the window overwrote the recorded answer AND scheduled a second advance - the quiz skipped a question and left it null, into calculateScores and the completion beacon. A data bug, not only a dead click. One guard closed both: a transitionLock ref (state alone is not a lock - two clicks in the same tick read the same render) plus disabled={isTransitioning} on the pills and back button, which is what makes Playwright wait out the key={currentStep} remount. Verified live: the double-click case that previously advanced 1->3 now lands on 2. Guard spec 8 passed, 1 flaky, 0 failed. The remaining flaky is a DIFFERENT bug - see nem-quiz-first-click-after-load-is-swallowed.

queue.title: Quiz: clicks before hydration are lost — the pills are live in the server-rendered HTML
queue.description: CONFIRMED and fixed 2026-08-20, awaiting a Webflow paste and a verification run. Webflow SERVER-RENDERS this component: the quiz markup, including the answer pills and question one's text, is in the static HTML before any JavaScript runs, and React hydrates it afterwards. The pills are therefore visible and clickable for a window before their handlers exist, and a click in that window is lost outright - it does not queue and it does not replay. Measured on staging over ten loads: ONE CLICK IN TEN was lost entirely, still lost with a twenty-second budget; on that run the element carried no React fiber or props key, while the nine that worked did and advanced in a consistent ~550ms. Fix: a hydrated flag set in a mount effect, gating disabled={isTransitioning || !hydrated} on the pills and the back button. It works because the server render happens with hydrated false, so the static markup ships disabled - the browser will not dispatch a click on a disabled button at all.
queue.note: Priority history worth keeping, because the reasoning went wrong twice. Filed P2 as a presumed hydration race. Bumped toward P1 on frequency, then the bump was WITHDRAWN after loadEventEnd measured ~8.3s in a browser with extensions, which made the hydration window look impossible to hit. That measurement was from an unrepresentative environment: in a clean context the page loads in ~550ms and hydration lands squarely in the click window. The original diagnosis was right and the falsification was wrong. Now P1 on evidence rather than on a hypothesis. LESSON: measure in an environment that resembles the one the bug appears in. The temporary probe that settled it is tests/acceptance/_probe-first-click.spec.js - re-run it after the paste to confirm zero lost clicks, then delete it.

queue.title: Opting in does not appear to send the second submit request
queue.description: The anonymous-completion design writes two rows per user against one token: a completion beacon at question 20, then an identified submission at opt-in. Establish first whether the request is genuinely not fired, or fired and failing validation client-side before dispatch - the opt-in form blocks submission on its own field validation, so a silently failing validation would look identical from the network side.

queue.title: Flat detection may be one point too wide, denying reports to users who should get one
queue.description: FLAT_SPREAD in nem-test-scoring.js is 3, so a profile whose highest and lowest mechanism scores differ by 3 is treated as flat - no mechanism named, no report, routed to the Tally contact link. Both worked examples in source doc section 4 describe the rule as 'within 2': example 4 (spread 4-2) and example 5 (spread 15-13) each say 'is 2 points - within 2, so nothing stands out'. If 2 is the rule, every spread-3 profile is currently being denied a report it should receive. ASK ALEX BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING: the normative sentence defining the flat threshold was not found in the captured text and may sit in a section that could not be retrieved, or in the generic 'NEM TEST source' doc. Two worked examples agreeing is suggestive, not definitive.
queue.note: Found 2026-08-20 reading Alex's source doc. P2 because it is unconfirmed, not because it is minor - if Alex confirms 'within 2' this becomes P1, since it means real users completing the test are being told there is nothing to report and pushed to a contact form instead of receiving the product. Note the direction of the error is the expensive one: too wide denies reports, too narrow would only give a weak report to someone who is genuinely undifferentiated. Changing FLAT_SPREAD to 2 is a one-line change plus the boundary tests in tests/nem/nem-test-scoring.test.js, which currently assert the 3 behaviour explicitly ('a spread of exactly FLAT_SPREAD is flat-high; one more is not') and would need updating with it.
